Analyze a resolvable row-column trial with RC, LV + RC or AR + RC models

Source: R/resolvable_row_column_analysis.R
analyze_resolvable_row_column.Rd

Fits the variance models of Williams, John and Whitaker (2006) by residual maximum likelihood (REML), with replicates and treatments fixed: $$E(y) = R\pi + X\tau,\quad var(y) = \sigma^2 V.$$

model = "rc"

The standard resolvable row-column mixed model: \(V = I + \eta_R P_R + \eta_C P_C\), i.e. random rows and columns within replicates.

model = "lv"

The two-dimensional linear variance model (LV + RC, Eq. 2): \(V = I + \eta_R P_R + \eta_C P_C - (\phi_R F_R + \phi_C F_C + \phi_{RC} F_{RC})\), with LV matrices for plots in the same row, in the same column, and in neither. lv_terms chooses which \(\phi\) terms are fitted and equal_phi = TRUE uses one \(\phi\) for rows and columns (square plots).

model = "ar"

Rows and columns plus a separable first-order autoregressive process (AR + RC, Eq. 4): \(V = I + \eta_R P_R + \eta_C P_C + \psi D(\rho_C) \otimes D(\rho_R)\) within replicates.

In every model the identity term is the independent error ("nugget"). With compare = TRUE the nested sequence RC, LV with one \(\phi\), LV with \(\phi_R, \phi_C\), LV with \(\phi_{RC}\) as well, and AR + RC are all fitted and compared by REML deviance (likelihood-ratio tests for the nested LV terms, and AIC), which is the sequential fitting process the paper recommends for deciding whether spatial terms are needed.

Usage

analyze_resolvable_row_column(
  data,
  response,
  model = c("rc", "lv", "ar"),
  lv_terms = c("phi_r", "phi_c"),
  equal_phi = FALSE,
  long_col = NULL,
  compare = TRUE,
  genotype_col = "all_entries",
  replicate_col = "replicate",
  row_col = "row_in_rep",
  col_col = "col_in_rep"
)

Arguments

data

A design data frame (for example design$design from resolvable_row_column_design()) or a design object, with a response.

response

Name of the numeric response column.

model

Variance model reported in adjusted_means: "rc", "lv", or "ar".

lv_terms

For model = "lv", the spatial terms to fit: any of "phi_r", "phi_c", "phi_rc".

equal_phi

Logical. For model = "lv", use a single \(\phi\) for rows and columns.

long_col

Optional name of a column with long-column (or long-row) labels to fit as fixed effects, as in latinized designs.

compare

Logical. If TRUE, also fit and compare the sequence of models.

genotype_col, replicate_col, row_col, col_col

Column names.

Value

An object of class resolvable_row_column_analysis, a list with

plot_results

One row per plot: the data, the fitted value (fixed effects plus the predicted row, column and spatial effects) and the residual \(V^{-1}(y - X\hat\beta)\).

adjusted_means

Treatment BLUEs (average over replicates) with standard errors, ranked best first.

variance_parameters

The REML estimates: \(\sigma^2\), the \(\eta\), \(\phi\), \(\psi\) and \(\rho\) parameters, and the implied row and column variance components \(\sigma^2\eta_R/s\) and \(\sigma^2\eta_C/k\).

model_comparison

With compare = TRUE, the deviance table.

anova

Intra-block ANOVA from the fixed model replicate + rows(replicate) + columns(replicate) + treatment.

diagnostics

REML deviance, number of variance parameters, mean SED and approximate 5% LSD.

Details

For latinized designs the long columns (or long rows) can be fitted as fixed effects with long_col.

References

Williams, E. R., John, J. A. and Whitaker, D. (2006). Construction of resolvable spatial row-column designs. Biometrics 62, 103-108. doi:10.1111/j.1541-0420.2005.00393.x

Examples

design <- resolvable_row_column_design(paste0("T", 1:20), 3, 4, 5,
                                       n_starts = 1, n_iter = 300, seed = 1)
trial <- design$design
set.seed(2)
trial$y <- 10 + 0.3 * trial$row + stats::rnorm(nrow(trial))
fit <- analyze_resolvable_row_column(trial, "y", model = "lv")
fit$model_comparison
#> # A tibble: 5 × 7
#>   model          n_variance_parameters deviance   AIC change_vs_rc compared_with

#> 2 RC + LV (sing…                     4     123.  131.         3.89 RC           
#> 3 RC + LV (phi_…                     5     121.  131.         5.46 RC           
#> 4 RC + LV (phi_…                     6     121.  133.         5.46 RC + LV (phi…
#> 5 RC + AR1 x AR1                     6     127.  139.         0    NA           
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: lrt_p_value <dbl>
head(fit$adjusted_means)
